Whether or not you have this one characteristic will make or break your success on a significant weightloss journey.

1. Eating too little — Your body needs enough food and energy to function properly. 2. Expecting overnight results — Healthy progress takes time, so be patient with yourself. 3. Ignoring your daily steps — Using a walking app can help you track your steps, stay motivated and work towards your daily movement goals! (I use Fastwalk) 4. Not drinking enough water — Keep a water bottle nearby and drink regularly throughout the day. 5. Doing workouts you hate — Find activities you genuinely enjoy so it’s easier to stay consistent. 6. Comparing your progress to others — Everyone’s body and journey are different, so focus on yourself. 7. Being too hard on yourself — Remember, consistency matters more than perfection. Give yourself grace! 💗 #gymtok #weightlosstips #glowuptips #motivation

Eating less isn't always the answer. For years, we've been told that if we want to lose weight, we need to eat less. So we skip meals, cut portions, avoid carbs and try to get by on as little food as possible. But here's where that approach can backfire, especially in midlife. When you're constantly trying to eat less, you're often missing out on the very things that make fat loss easier to manage. Protein to help keep you full and maintain muscle. Fibre to support digestion, gut health and keep hunger in check. Food volume, so you can eat satisfying meals without consuming excessive calories. And when you're hungry all the time, it's much harder to stick to your calorie goals. You end up snacking, picking at food or overeating later in the day. The answer isn't to keep cutting calories. It's to make the calories you're eating work harder for you. Build your meals around protein, add plenty of fibre-rich foods and fill your plate with foods that give you more volume for fewer calories. You still need a calorie deficit to lose fat, but you don't need to spend your days feeling hungry and deprived. Eating smarter, not just eating less, can make all the difference. Y’all will forever hear me screaming that the number on the scale doesn’t tell the whole story 🗣️‼️ You can lose weight without losing much body fat and you can lose body fat without seeing a huge change on the scale 🤭  Which is exactly why I encourage looking at progress from multiple angles instead of letting one number determine whether what you’re doing is working babe  Your measurements, progress photos, strength in the gym, how your clothes fit, and your weight trends over time can all help paint a better picture of what’s happening with your body 👏🏻 (ESPECIALLY if your goal is body recomposition!!)
